title: Life interval
description: What the life stage writes: for one fill or piece and one history layer, a span of years in which the layer runs at one speed from one clock. The layer's value at a date is the texel's drive applied to its material's curve, run at rate / 1000 of the thing's speed over (date - clock): an amplitude times the curve, or a rate into it, as the layer's law in schemas/layers.json says (decisions D5.1). The clock is resetYear, or the reach's date where a texel is within the reach. The pages' drives and the piece table's clocks are baked from these; no texel holds an offset, and the piece table keeps the age a piece brought in whole years (D5.4). Care is not an interval: it is the thing's, read as a uniform. All integers: years and months, per mille.

on.description: The fill or piece it is about. A replaced part is a new fill and so starts its own intervals.

to.description: Null while it still runs at the fabric date.

resetYear.description: The year the layer last started from nothing: the stone laid (placed, for polish), the face bared or cleaned (bare, for lichen and moss: placed less the age brought), the coat put on.

rate.description: Per mille of the material's own rate: 1000 runs the curve as the material record gives it.

ageOffsetMonths.description: Age the surface brought with it, in months: a reclaimed stone's years in the heap. The piece table holds it in whole years, so a stone's is a multiple of 12. A layer that starts late takes its material's delay (layers.json), not an offset.

reach.description: Optional: a disturbance that restarts part of the fill, the texels within its reach. hands: a piece lifted by hands, whose lichen at the hands' reach (from the face kind and edge distance) runs from here. bed: the bed relaid, whose moss runs from here where the page's bed reach (h1.a) is 1.

cause.description: The event that lifted the piece or relaid its bed.
The event or rule that started this interval (a works campaign, a change of use, a gutter that failed; never care, which is a uniform).
